dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Four hours. The ceiling has a water stain shaped like an island. Some mornings it's Java. Some mornings it's nothing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (One year today. Nobody's going to say it. That's fine. That's the deal.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Fiz. I can hear your alarm through the wall. It's been going for eleven minutes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not gonna write you up. I'm just gonna stand here judging you until you turn it off.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She does this. Checks on me like I'm something she's responsible for. I don't know how to tell her that helps.)

choices.choice_text: "You've been up since five, haven't you."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Hall check's in ten. And Fiz — eat something today. Not the vending machine. Something with a shape.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Headphones. Aura. The Strokes. The same song I've played four hundred times because it's the only thing that makes the noise in my head line up straight.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Somewhere between the door and the stairs my brain runs the thing again. A hallway. Someone raising a gun. Me, calm. Always calm, in the version where it happens.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Nobody's ever raised anything at me. My head just likes rehearsing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: There he is. My most reliable customer and my worst tipper.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Sit. Booth by the window's still got heat in it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She always remembers. Even when the rest of the town tries to forget.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: You know this place used to be packed at seven? Line out the door. Fishermen, truckers, half the school skipping first period.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Now it's you, Brandon back there, and whoever's lost on the coast road.

choices.choice_text: [Look at the half-burned photo behind the counter.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Oh, honey. Everything changed. That's the whole answer and nobody in this town will give you a longer one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Eat your eggs.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Brandon Montgomery
dialogue_sequence.text: You keep looking at that picture.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He hasn't moved in twenty minutes. I didn't think he was awake.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Brandon Montgomery
dialogue_sequence.text: Everyone does, first year. Then they stop. You'll stop.

choices.choice_text: [Say nothing. Go back to your coffee.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (You can hear Amber before you can see her. That's the point of Amber.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: OH MY GOD, everyone — everyone, look who decided to bring the same jacket for the fourth day running!

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: Riley! Riley, look at me. Look at the light, babe, I need your eyes in it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Amber. Get the fucking phone out of my face.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Lila West
dialogue_sequence.text: Ooh. She talks. Write it down, someone write it down.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: Enough, Lila. She's already embarrassing herself, you don't need to hold her hand through it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's the trick. Zoey never throws the punch. She just stands close enough to be in the photo.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jake Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Hey. Exchange student. You dropped something.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: He didn't drop anything, man.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jake Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: He dropped his fucking passport, Luke. That was the joke. God.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The hallway is doing the thing where it gets quiet and everybody keeps walking. Nobody looks. That's the town in one hallway.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (My hands are shaking. Not from fear. From having nowhere to put it.)

choices.choice_text: "That was a shit joke, Jake. Even Luke didn't get it."
[Say nothing. Do nothing. Let it pass.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You didn't have to do that.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...I'm glad you did. But you didn't have to.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Owen Rhys
dialogue_sequence.text: Assignment. Due Friday. One image. Here's the brief, and I want you to sit with it before you groan at me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Owen Rhys
dialogue_sequence.text: Photograph something this town would rather you didn't look at.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ezra Lang
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not a brief, that's a mood board.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Owen Rhys
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a brief, Ezra. You just don't like ones you can't win on technique.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: I've been shooting near the old lighthouse. There's a light down there that doesn't behave.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: I mean the fog does something to it. Obviously. I'm not being weird.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She said it like she was taking it back before anyone made her.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ezra Lang
dialogue_sequence.text: Fiz shoots the lighthouse constantly. Might want to pick something else, Sienna. He gets precious about his spots.

choices.choice_text: "Shoot it. I'd like to see your version."
[Let Ezra have it. Look at the brief.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You'll get marked down, you know.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: Not by him. By whoever reads it after him. Nobody here grades honesty well.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Olivia. She's been sitting two seats over all semester and this is the fourth thing she's ever said to me.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (All four have been correct.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: Because I grew up here and I'd rather be marked down than pretend.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You should come out to the cliffs sometime. It's not a line. I just think you'd like the quiet.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: Heard about the hallway. Heard Jake tried a passport joke and ate shit on it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Mason.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: What? I'm proud of him. Our boy's developing a mouth.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Yeah, and Jake's developing a grudge. Those aren't the same thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: Guys — guys, hold on, I'm live. Say hi to the Grid!

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: This is Fiz. He edits my thumbnails and he has never once said hello to chat. Fiz. FIZ. Four hundred people.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Kieran pushes his fries into the middle of the table. He does this every day. We have never discussed it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: Wrote something on my board this morning. "The town rebuilt everything except the part that remembers."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't know if it's good. Don't really care.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: That's depressing as hell, man.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: It's not wrong, though.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Pete's brother. Ten years this month. Nobody says it, and Pete keeps eating like the sentence didn't come out of him.)

choices.choice_text: [Change the subject. Give him the exit.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You brought the camera.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You always bring the camera when you're working something out. You know that, right?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I didn't know that.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Theo asked about you last night. First question he's asked me in about a week.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: He wanted to know if you actually listen or if you're just quiet. I said both. He thought that was funny.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She talks about her brother the way people talk about something they're carrying up a hill.)

choices.choice_text: [Frame a shot of the ruins instead.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Nobody asks me that. Do you know how weird that is? Everyone asks about Theo. Or Dad. Or the house.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You're the only person who doesn't ask me for something first.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's twisting the bracelet. The silver one. Her mother's. She does that when she's deciding whether to say a true thing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't go down to the water line. I mean it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I don't do water. At all. I know it's stupid.

choices.choice_text: [Step back from the edge without being asked twice.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Nothing happened. I was six. Everyone in this town has a water thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's the second time today someone's answered a question by describing the whole town instead of themselves.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I take the shot anyway. Ruins, fog, the water going grey behind it. 4:41 PM. I remember because the light was dying and I checked.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You went out there.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You've got cliff mud on your shoes and you look like you're still standing in it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's not smug about it. She just says things.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: My mother drowned near the docks during the evacuation. Nineteen years old, I've had ten years to say that sentence, and people still flinch.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You didn't.

choices.choice_text: [Sit down next to her. Say nothing.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: No. That's the point. Everybody in this place has decided grief is a thing you do quietly and then stop.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not being dark. I'm being accurate. There's a difference and nobody here can tell.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Steps close at six, you two.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Calder. Go on.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He waits until she's gone. He wanted me on my own.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: You were out at the cliffs.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Not asking. I do rounds, I know what mud looks like.

choices.choice_text: [Show him the camera. Nothing to hide.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Kid. I'm not confiscating anything. I've never confiscated anything off you and I've had eleven chances.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Careful where you point that thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Not a threat. I've been threatened. This was the other thing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: Rowe left the lab key with me. Don't tell anyone, he'll stop doing it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: You cutting the lighthouse stuff? I'll shut up. I know you don't like people over your shoulder.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Two hours. The good kind. The kind where the noise finally has somewhere to go.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Clip four. The wide of the ruins. I've watched it eleven times because something in it keeps pulling my eye and I can't name what.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Timecode 00:04:41. Fog rolling left to right across the frame.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Then, for eleven frames — less than half a second — it rolls right to left. Same fog. Same shot. No cut.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I step it frame by frame. There's no seam. No dropped frames. The timecode doesn't skip. It's continuous footage and the weather goes backwards inside it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: You've gone grey, man. What.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: ...I mean. Codec's doing something weird? Interlacing, maybe. Cheap sensor in fog, it happens.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not — that's not what that is, is it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He's giving me a rational answer. He's giving it to himself, really.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: My sister was a student here. In 2013.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not saying those are related. I'm saying I'm going home now.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (2:14 AM. I've watched it ninety times. It doesn't get less true.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There are four rational explanations. I've tested three. The fourth is that I'm wrong about what I'm seeing, which is the one I'd like, so I don't trust it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A year of being polite. A year of not asking. Linda changing the subject. Riley stepping back from the water. Marcus saying careful. Sienna taking it back before anyone made her.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I thought this town was quiet. It isn't quiet. It's holding its breath.)

choices.choice_text: [Back it up three times. Tell no one. Start looking.]
[Delete it. Go to sleep. Be a guest here.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("I guess if bad shit happens I should just let it happen.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I've been telling myself that for a year. Tonight it sounds like something a coward says.)
